–Lens–An optical device with near-perfect symmetry that is able to transmit and focus/bend electromagnetic radiation–Shape of the lens determines the direction the radiation will bend–Microscopy: Rays (waves) of radiation pass through a lens and converge (come together) at a specific distance from the lens–Known as focal length

Focal Length
explanation: This slide defines a lens as an optical device with near-perfect symmetry that can transmit and focus/bend electromagnetic radiation. The specific shape of the lens dictates the direction in which the radiation bends. In microscopy, rays (waves) of radiation pass through a lens and converge (come together) at a specific distance from the lens. This distance is defined as the focal length.

questions.q: What is a lens and what determines the direction in which radiation bends through it?
opts: A device that blocks light; its color determines the bend.
An optical device with near-perfect symmetry that transmits and focus/bends radiation; its shape determines the direction of bending.
A detector that gathers data; its distance from the eye determines the direction.
A source of radiation; its voltage determines the direction.
